chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the apostate, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who desires away from Islam and disbelieves in what Allah revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) after his Islam, so there is no repentance for him, and his killing becomes obligatory, and his wife is divorced from him, and what he leaves is distributed among his children.'

key_terms.فَلَا تَوْبَةَ لَهُ: So there is no repentance for him

ai.seo_question: What are the legal consequences of apostasy in Shia Islam regarding repentance, execution, marriage, and inheritance?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the definitive ruling of the second Imam, Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), regarding the murtadd who rejects Islam after embracing it. It specifies that such apostasy precludes repentance (tawbah), mandates execution (qatl), and results in the immediate severance of marital ties (fanāʾ al-nikāḥ), with the deceased's estate distributed to his children. This ruling highlights the severity of apostasy in Shia fiqh as a breach of the covenant of faith, distinct from mere doubt or temporary hesitation.
